premise: Maya radios hello to Earth through the satellite and hears only silence, so she says it again and again — and every hello comes back, one after another, just a little late.
inspiration: Ovid's Echo, turned: the echo is family a long way off, and it answers every single hello.
lesson: Patience: some answers are worth the wait.
learning: A radio message takes a little over a second to travel between the Moon and the Earth.

en-US.title: Hello, Earth!
en-US.text: {satellite:float loop 0.3} {woman:enter} Maya wanted to say hello to her family on Earth. High above, the {satellite:enter} satellite {satellite:live hold} turned toward home, a little light glowing. {sfx:beep} Beep. {woman:face happy} {woman:says} “Hello, Earth!” [short pause] Nothing. {woman:face surprised} {woman:says} “Hello?” Nothing at all. {woman:says} [rushed] “Hello? Hello! HELLO!” {man:enter} Leo loped over, {man:face happy} trying very hard not to laugh. {man:says} “Patience. Even radio needs time to get there.” {man:live} He tapped his wrist display. A little over a second to reach the Earth. A little over a second to come back. {sfx:crackle solo} And then, one after another, the answers arrived: “Hello, Maya!” “Hello?” “Hello!” “HELLO!” [laughs] {woman:face happy} {woman:wobble x2} Maya laughed so hard she had to sit down. {satellite:live resume} Up above, the satellite kept the line open, one patient second at a time.

es-ES.title: ¡Hola, Tierra!
es-ES.text: {satellite:float loop 0.3} {woman:enter} Maya quería saludar a su familia en la Tierra. Muy alto, el {satellite:enter} satélite {satellite:live hold} se giró hacia casa, con una lucecita encendida. {sfx:beep} Bip. {woman:face happy} {woman:says} «¡Hola, Tierra!» [short pause] Nada. {woman:face surprised} {woman:says} «¿Hola?» Nada de nada. {woman:says} [rushed] «¿Hola? ¡Hola! ¡HOLA!» {man:enter} Leo llegó dando saltos, {man:face happy} aguantándose la risa. {man:says} «Paciencia. Hasta la radio tarda en llegar.» {man:live} Dio unos toquecitos a la pantalla de su muñeca. Algo más de un segundo hasta la Tierra. Algo más de un segundo de vuelta. {sfx:crackle solo} Y entonces, una detrás de otra, llegaron las respuestas: «¡Hola, Maya!» «¿Hola?» «¡Hola!» «¡HOLA!» [laughs] {woman:face happy} {woman:wobble x2} Maya se rió tanto que tuvo que sentarse. {satellite:live resume} Allá arriba, el satélite mantuvo la línea abierta, segundo a segundo, con paciencia.

beep.prompt: a single soft electronic radio beep, clean and friendly

crackle.prompt: a short soft crackle of a radio channel opening, gentle static fading in and out
